turns.text: quick q. what keywords do network tech postings usually list, and how do i tell must-haves from nice-to-haves in a job description. just checking other servers rn lol

Common keywords in network technician postings:

**Core skills:** TCP/IP, DHCP, DNS, VLANs, subnetting, routing and switching, LAN/WAN, Wi-Fi/wireless troubleshooting, VPN, firewalls
**Tools and gear:** Cisco/Meraki/Aruba/Ubiquiti, network monitoring (SolarWinds, PRTG, Nagios), ticketing systems (ServiceNow, Jira), cabling and patch panels
**Certs:** CompTIA Network+ (most common entry level), CCNA, sometimes Security+
**Soft/process terms:** documentation, escalation, vendor management, on-call, SLAs, change management

**Reading must-haves vs nice-to-haves:**
- Must-haves: "required," "must have," "minimum qualifications," and anything in the first few bullets of a list
- Nice-to-haves: "preferred," "a plus," "ideally," "familiarity with," "or equivalent experience"
- Years of experience are often soft. If you hit about 70% of the required list, apply anyway
- A cert listed as "or working toward" usually means in-progress counts

Want me to match these against your own experience once you paste a posting?
